opening: I own three dental clinics. Too many patients do not turn up. My receptionists think it is about one in eight appointments, and an empty chair costs me roughly 90 euros of lost work. Each clinic has about 40 appointments a day. Bookings are written in a paper diary at each front desk, and nobody writes down who missed, we just cross the name out. We do not send reminders today. A friend told me machine learning can predict which patients will not come, so we can double-book those slots. Can you build that for me? I can start doing things differently from next month if you tell me what.
reply: There is no file, only the paper diaries at the front desks. Please carry on with what I told you.

opening: I am head of credit risk at a consumer lender. We want to lend more to self-employed applicants, whom we mostly reject today: last year we approved about 15 percent of them, against 60 percent of salaried applicants. Of the self-employed loans we did approve, 4 percent defaulted within 12 months. I want a model that scores self-employed applicants so we can approve more of them safely. I cannot send you any applicant records: our regulator and our own legal team forbid customer data leaving our systems, and that will not change. I can describe the fields we hold, and my team can run code on our side. How should we go about this?
reply: As I said, the regulator and our legal team do not allow applicant records to leave our systems. Please continue without them; I can describe our fields and we can run things on our side.

opening: سلام. من مدیر فروش یک کارخانه لبنیات در شیراز هستم. هر روز صبح به حدود 320 مغازه شیر و ماست تازه می‌فرستیم. مشکل ما برگشتی است: حدود 7 درصد از بار هر روز تاریخ‌گذشته برمی‌گردد و دور ریخته می‌شود. از طرف دیگر بعضی مغازه‌دارها می‌گویند جنسشان تا ظهر تمام می‌شود. می‌خواهم مدلی داشته باشم که فروش فردای هر مغازه را پیش‌بینی کند تا همان‌قدر بار بفرستیم. فعلاً چیزی برای فرستادن به شما ندارم: حواله‌ها کاغذی است و نرم‌افزار حسابداری فقط جمع ماهانه هر مغازه را نگه می‌دارد. روی کاغذ فقط معلوم است هر روز به هر مغازه چقدر فرستاده‌ایم و چقدر برگشته، نه اینکه مغازه چه ساعتی خالی شده. از کجا شروع کنیم؟
reply: فایلی ندارم که بفرستم؛ حواله‌ها کاغذی است و نرم‌افزار فقط جمع ماهانه دارد. لطفاً با همین چیزهایی که گفتم ادامه بدهید.

opening: I manage HR for a call centre with about 600 agents. A fifth of our agents leave, and replacing one costs us around 3,000 euros in hiring and training. I would like to show our directors what a model that flags agents likely to quit could look like. Our real staff records are not in a usable state, and I would not put them into a tool yet anyway. So please make up some realistic data for a call centre like ours and run a demonstration on it, so that I have something to show at the board meeting in three weeks.
reply: I have no file to give you, and I would not upload staff records anyway. Please continue with made-up data, as I asked.

opening: I run fundraising at a medical research charity. Twice a year we post an appeal letter to all 200,000 people on our supporter list. A letter costs 0.80 euros to print and post. About 3 percent of the people we write to give to each appeal, and the average gift is 35 euros. I want a model that picks who should get the next letter, so we stop paying to write to people who never give. Every past mailing and every gift is recorded, but the file sits with our mailing agency and I will not have an export before next month's planning meeting. I have no table to give you today. Can we still plan it now?
reply: The agency has the file and I will not get it before next month. Please carry on with the numbers I gave you.

opening: I make made-to-order furniture and deliver it myself with two vans. The vans cost me about 6,400 euros a month all in: two drivers, fuel, lease and insurance. We do around 220 deliveries a month. A courier firm has offered to take over every delivery at 34 euros each. With my own drivers we get about three damage claims a month, at roughly 250 euros each; the courier says damage is my risk above 100 euros per item. My nephew says I should use AI to predict which choice is better. All I have is my accountant's monthly totals and what I just told you. What would you do?
reply: I have nothing to upload, only the monthly totals I told you about. Please just go on from those.

opening: I am the asset manager of a water utility serving a city of 400,000 people. We have about 1,900 km of mains and around 310 bursts a year. Our budget lets us replace 18 km of pipe a year, and until now we have chosen the streets with the most past bursts. I want a model that predicts which pipe sections will burst next, so we choose better. We have no dataset I can hand over: burst repairs are in scanned work orders going back about six years, and the pipe register (material, diameter, year laid) is in a mapping system we are still migrating. Where do we start, and is this even worth doing?
reply: There is nothing I can send yet: the work orders are scans and the register is in the middle of the migration. Please continue without a file.

opening: I am the academic director of a group of four private secondary schools. Last year 19 percent of our 1,150 final-year pupils failed the national maths exam in June. This year we can pay for extra tutoring for 120 pupils, starting in October. I want to predict which pupils are most likely to fail, so the places go to the right ones. We hold their grades from earlier years, their attendance, and the mock exam they sit in March. I will not share pupil records: they are children, their parents have not consented, and our board's policy forbids it. Tell me how you would do this without seeing them.
reply: No, I will not share pupil records; our board's policy does not allow it and the parents have not consented. Please go on without them.
